learning_goal: Explain why the embryo folds in the median plane during week 4, draw the head fold and the tail fold in sagittal section, list in order what each fold carries and where it ends up — including the reversal that puts the heart caudal to the oropharyngeal membrane — and use those movements to account for ectopia cordis, a diaphragmatic hernia and caudal regression.

structures.name: Where we start — a flat trilaminar disc
structures.label: Where we start — a flat trilaminar disc
structures.narration: At the end of week three the embryo is a flat, pear-shaped disc of three layers, with the amniotic cavity above it and the yolk sac hanging below. Nothing about that shape looks like a body yet. Everything in this scene is how that disc becomes a curled, cylindrical embryo in the space of about a week.

structures.name: Cut it in the median plane and watch from the side
structures.label: Cut it in the median plane and watch from the side
structures.narration: Cranio-caudal folding happens in the median plane, so draw it as a side view. One long cut from head end to tail end, and the same picture repeated at each stage. Lateral folding is the other plane and is a separate scene; if you try to draw both in one diagram you will confuse yourself and the examiner.

structures.name: Why it folds — the nervous system outgrows the disc
structures.label: Why it folds — the nervous system outgrows the disc
structures.narration: Folding is not an act of will. The neural tube — especially the brain vesicles at the head end — grows extremely fast, while the yolk sac attached underneath barely grows at all. A sheet that grows quickly along its length while anchored below has only one option: it curls. That is the whole mechanism.

structures.name: And the amnion presses in from outside
structures.label: And the amnion presses in from outside
structures.narration: At the same time the amniotic cavity expands until it wraps around the embryo from every side. So the disc is pushed from within by growth and drawn round from without by the enlarging amnion. Where the amnion finally meets underneath is where the umbilical cord will be.

structures.name: The head fold — the cranial end swings ventrally
structures.label: The head fold — the cranial end swings ventrally
structures.narration: The cranial end of the disc grows forward past its own attachment and then curls downwards, so the future head comes to overhang the front of the embryo. Draw it as the top of a question mark. Everything that was lying flat in front of the head is now swung underneath it — and that is the part students get wrong.

structures.name: Before the fold: the order from head backwards
structures.label: Before the fold: the order from head backwards
structures.narration: Learn this list in order, from the cranial edge working back: septum transversum, then the pericardial cavity, then the cardiogenic area with the heart tubes in it, then the oropharyngeal membrane, then the neural plate. That is the flat-disc order, and it is the only thing you have to memorise here — the fold does the rest.

structures.name: After the fold: the order is reversed
structures.label: After the fold: the order is reversed
terms: septum transversum caudal to the heart
structures.narration: Now rotate that strip through half a turn, which is exactly what the head fold does to it. The oropharyngeal membrane ends up most cranial, the heart lies ventral and behind it, and the septum transversum ends up caudal to the heart, where the diaphragm will be. The list has flipped end for end. If you can reproduce that reversal you have understood cranio-caudal folding.

structures.name: Before the fold: septum transversum, at the cranial edge
structures.label: Septum transversum — before the fold, most cranial
structures.narration: On the flat disc the septum transversum is the most cranial of the four — at the cranial edge, in front of the cardiogenic area. This is the same part as the one in the folded panel beside it, drawn where it starts.

structures.name: Before the fold: the pericardial cavity
structures.label: Pericardial cavity — before the fold, the space the cardiogenic area lies in
structures.narration: The pericardial cavity on the flat disc, caudal to the septum transversum and around the cardiogenic area. Drawn opened, as it is in the folded panel.

structures.name: Before the fold: the cardiogenic area with the heart tube in it
structures.label: Cardiogenic area — before the fold, between the septum transversum and the membrane
terms: heart tube on the flat disc
structures.narration: The cardiogenic area, with the heart tube in it, lies CRANIAL to the oropharyngeal membrane on the flat disc. That is the half of this topic students get wrong, and it is what this panel exists to show.

structures.name: Before the fold: the oropharyngeal membrane
structures.label: Oropharyngeal membrane — before the fold, most caudal of the four
structures.narration: On the flat disc the oropharyngeal membrane lies CAUDAL to the cardiogenic area and the septum transversum — the opposite of where it ends up. After the fold it is the most cranial point of the embryo.

structures.name: The head fold pinches off the foregut
structures.label: The head fold pinches off the foregut
structures.narration: As the head curls, the dorsal part of the yolk sac is taken into the embryo as a blind tube — the foregut. Its cranial end is sealed by the oropharyngeal membrane, with the stomodeum, the future mouth, as a dimple on the other side. That membrane breaks down in week four and the gut opens to the amniotic cavity for the first time.

structures.name: The septum transversum is carried down to the diaphragm
structures.label: The septum transversum is carried down to the diaphragm
structures.narration: The septum transversum starts at the cranial edge of the disc, opposite the future neck, and the head fold drags it back and down towards the thorax. That single journey explains a fact you were told to memorise: the diaphragm is supplied by C3, C4 and C5, because its central tendon was innervated while it still lay at cervical level and the phrenic nerve simply grew longer to follow it.

structures.name: The tail fold — the caudal end swings ventrally too
structures.label: The tail fold — the caudal end swings ventrally too
structures.narration: The same thing happens at the other end. The caudal region grows past its attachment and curls forwards and under, so the tail end also comes to point towards the belly. The embryo now has the C-shape you see in every week-four picture.

structures.name: The tail fold pinches off the hindgut and the cloaca
structures.label: The tail fold pinches off the hindgut and the cloaca
structures.narration: At the tail end the yolk sac contributes the hindgut, ending blindly at the cloacal membrane. The allantois, which ran into the connecting stalk, is drawn in with it, so the terminal hindgut becomes the cloaca — the common chamber that will later be partitioned into rectum in front of one wall and bladder and urethra in front of the other.

structures.name: The connecting stalk is swung to the ventral surface
structures.label: The connecting stalk is swung to the ventral surface
structures.narration: The connecting stalk began behind the tail end of the disc. The tail fold carries it round onto the ventral surface, where it meets the narrowing yolk stalk and is sheathed by amnion — and that combination is the umbilical cord. The cloacal membrane travels round with it and ends up on the ventral surface too, which is why an infra-umbilical wall defect and a bladder problem are the same accident.

structures.name: What is left in the middle — the midgut
structures.label: What is left in the middle — the midgut
structures.narration: The two folds seal the gut at each end but leave the middle open. The midgut stays in wide communication with the yolk sac, and the connection narrows into the vitelline duct. So the three parts of the primitive gut are simply a consequence of geometry: sealed in front by the head fold, sealed behind by the tail fold, still open in the middle. The gut tube itself is taught in its own scene.

structures.name: The result — a C-shaped embryo with a tube inside it
structures.label: The result — a C-shaped embryo with a tube inside it
structures.narration: Put the two folds together and the flat disc has become a curled cylinder, dorsally convex, with a gut tube running through it and a single narrow stalk at the belly. In under a week the embryo has acquired a head end, a tail end, a front and a back, and everything after this is refinement of that body plan.

structures.name: Head fold fails — ectopia cordis
structures.label: Head fold fails — ectopia cordis
terms: failure of ventral body wall closure
structures.narration: If the cranial part of the ventral wall never closes, the heart is left on the outside of the chest — ectopia cordis. In its full form it comes with four companions as the pentalogy of Cantrell: a sternal cleft, a midline epigastric omphalocele, a defect in the front of the diaphragm, a pericardial defect and an intracardiac malformation. Name it from the picture and you have named the failed fold.

structures.name: Septum transversum fails — congenital diaphragmatic hernia
structures.label: Septum transversum fails — congenital diaphragmatic hernia
structures.narration: The septum transversum is only the front part of the diaphragm; the rest has to close behind it. When the posterolateral gap stays open — usually on the left — abdominal contents climb into the chest. That is a Bochdalek hernia. The baby is born in respiratory distress with a scaphoid abdomen, and the danger is not the hole but the lung that never had room to grow.

structures.name: Tail fold fails — caudal regression
structures.label: Tail fold fails — caudal regression
structures.narration: Deficient mesoderm at the caudal end gives caudal regression syndrome: absent or shortened sacrum, lower limb weakness, a neurogenic bladder, anorectal and renal malformations, and in its extreme form sirenomelia with fused lower limbs. The association to remember for the exam is poorly controlled maternal diabetes. It is the single most quoted teratogenic link in this topic.

structures.name: Neural tube
structures.label: The neural tube along the dorsal midline
structures.narration: The neural tube runs the whole length of the embryo along its dorsal midline, and it is the sheet that grows. Draw it first in any sagittal picture of folding: everything else in this scene is arranged around it, and the fold is what happens to a sheet anchored below a structure that lengthens above.

structures.name: Oropharyngeal membrane
structures.label: The oropharyngeal membrane — the future mouth
structures.narration: Where ectoderm meets endoderm with no mesoderm between them, the two layers stay fused as the oropharyngeal membrane. Follow it: it starts well back from the cranial edge of the disc, and after the head fold it is the most cranial point of the whole embryo. It ruptures in week four and the gut opens to the amniotic cavity.

structures.name: Heart tube
structures.label: The heart tube in the cardiogenic area
structures.narration: The heart tubes form in the cardiogenic area, which on the flat disc lies CRANIAL to the oropharyngeal membrane. Watch where it ends up. After the head fold the heart lies ventral to the foregut and caudal to that membrane, in the cardiac prominence you can see on the outside of any week-four embryo.

structures.name: Pericardial cavity
structures.label: The pericardial cavity around the heart
structures.narration: The pericardial cavity is the space the heart tube lies in, and it travels with the heart through the fold. It is drawn here as an opened sac so the heart inside it can be seen; the coelom and how it is partitioned belong to their own scene.

structures.name: Cloacal membrane
structures.label: The cloacal membrane
structures.narration: The cloacal membrane is the tail end's counterpart of the oropharyngeal membrane: ectoderm fused to endoderm, sealing the hindgut. On the flat disc it faces caudally. After the tail fold it faces the belly, which is why a defect below the umbilicus and a bladder that fails to close are the same accident.

structures.name: Cloaca
structures.label: The cloaca — the common terminal chamber
structures.narration: The terminal hindgut dilates where the allantois joins it, and that common chamber is the cloaca. It is later partitioned by the urorectal septum into rectum behind and bladder and urethra in front; that partition is taught elsewhere and is not drawn here.

structures.name: Allantois
structures.label: The allantois, drawn in with the tail fold
structures.narration: The allantois is a finger of endoderm that runs from the caudal gut into the connecting stalk. The tail fold draws it in, so it opens into the cloaca; its remnant in the adult is the urachus, and then the median umbilical ligament.

structures.name: Vitelline duct
structures.label: The vitelline duct — what the wide connection narrows to
structures.narration: At the start the midgut and the yolk sac are one continuous space. As the folds close in from both ends the communication narrows to a single duct running in the cord. Its failure to disappear is a Meckel diverticulum, which is that entry's work and not this one's.

structures.name: Yolk sac
structures.label: The yolk sac, which barely grows
structures.narration: The yolk sac hangs below the disc and does almost nothing. That is exactly why the embryo folds: a sheet that lengthens fast while it stays anchored to something that does not has no option but to curl around it.

views.title: Why a flat disc has to curl

ops.kind: grows far faster than, forcing it to curl

views.narration: Start with the flat trilaminar disc and ask one question: what would make a flat sheet curl? Two things. The neural tube along its midline grows enormously while the yolk sac below it does not, and the amniotic cavity swells around the whole embryo. Growth from inside, pressure from outside, and the disc folds in both planes at once. This scene follows the median plane.

claims.claim: the disc is FLAT: it is far wider across than it is deep
and nothing has folded yet
the flat-disc order holds: septum transversum, then heart, then the membrane

views.title: Halfway: both ends on their way round
views.narration: Stop the clock halfway. Both ends have swung about a quarter turn and neither has finished: the cranial end is still reaching forward rather than tucking under, the caudal end is following it, and the connection between midgut and yolk sac is still wide. Nothing here is a separate event from the last picture or the next one — it is the same movement, caught in the middle.
views.new_narration: Added by the 2026-09-30 re-author. A process scene that shows only its endpoints teaches the endpoints; this beat exists so the two folds are seen as one continuous movement. No existing narration was altered and no beat was removed.

claims.claim: the cranial strip has turned about half of its half-turn
the section is part way from flat to round
and the connection to the yolk sac is still wide

views.title: The head fold, and the reversal it causes
views.narration: Before the fold, working back from the cranial edge: septum transversum, pericardial cavity, cardiogenic area, oropharyngeal membrane. The head fold swings that whole strip through half a turn. Afterwards the oropharyngeal membrane is most cranial, the heart lies ventral and caudal to it, and the septum transversum sits behind the heart at the future diaphragm. Same four things, opposite order. Draw both panels side by side and the reversal teaches itself.

claims.claim: the order has flipped end for end: membrane most cranial, then heart, then septum
and the oropharyngeal membrane IS the most cranial point
the strip has turned through half a turn

views.title: Walk the strip through the fold
views.narration: Now walk it, one stop at a time. The strip as it lay on the flat disc; the fold that takes hold of it; and the strip where that fold has carried it to. Nothing is redrawn between the first stop and the last — the same material stations are bent round, which is why the oropharyngeal membrane ends up at the crown and the septum transversum ends up behind the heart.

claims.claim: the oropharyngeal membrane's own facing has come through a quarter turn
the membrane has passed the septum transversum, so the strip's two ends have changed places
and the strip as a whole has turned further than half a turn, further than the septum alone

pinned_ok.head_order_before: DELIBERATE, and it is the first stop of the walk: head_order_before is the cranial strip pinned at t = 0 and head_order_after the same part at t = 1, so the walk starts on the strip as it lay flat and ends on the strip as the fold left it. Same reason as beat 3, which this beat was split from.
pinned_ok.flat_disc: DELIBERATE, and for the same reason as on beat 3: the first stop needs the disc the strip lay on, or it is a rod floating in space next to a folded embryo. Drawn opened in the median plane like the rest of the scene.

views.title: The foregut appears, and the diaphragm starts its journey

ops.kind: takes the dorsal yolk sac into the embryo as

views.narration: Cut in the midline and watch the head fold roll the dorsal part of the yolk sac into the embryo. That blind tube is the foregut, sealed in front by the oropharyngeal membrane until it ruptures in week four. In the same movement the septum transversum is carried from opposite the neck down towards the thorax — which is why the diaphragm answers to C3, C4 and C5 and why the phrenic nerve is so long.

claims.claim: a third of the gut is now sealed foregut
and the septum transversum has been carried a long way caudally
with the heart ventral to the membrane it used to lie cranial of

views.title: The tail fold does the mirror image
views.narration: The tail end curls the same way. It seals the hindgut at the cloacal membrane, pulls the allantois in so that the terminal hindgut becomes the cloaca, and swings the connecting stalk from behind the embryo round onto its belly. The cloacal membrane travels with it. Every one of those three movements is an exam answer somewhere else in the course.

claims.claim: the cloacal membrane has come round to face the belly
a third of the gut is sealed hindgut
and the connecting stalk points ventrally

views.title: What the two folds leave behind
views.narration: Sealed in front, sealed behind, still open in the middle. That is all foregut, midgut and hindgut means at this stage, and the midgut keeps its connection to the yolk sac through the narrowing vitelline duct. Step back and look at the embryo: a curled cylinder with a gut tube inside it and one stalk at the belly, where a flat disc stood a week ago.

claims.claim: the wide connection has narrowed several-fold into the vitelline duct
and it is still open — the midgut never seals
the section is round: the disc has become a cylinder

views.title: The C-shaped embryo, from outside
views.narration: Now close the embryo up and look at it from the side, the way an ultrasound or a textbook plate shows it. Dorsally convex, curled around a belly that has one stalk leaving it, with the head overhanging the heart at one end and the tail tucked under at the other. Every feature of that outline was produced by the two movements in this scene, and none of it was there a week ago.
views.new_narration: Added by the 2026-09-30 re-author, because no existing beat shows the finished outside of the embryo and the learning goal asks a student to draw it. No existing narration was altered.

claims.claim: the tail fold has turned the caudal end through most of a right angle and more
the brain vesicles have hugely outgrown the rest of the neural tube

views.title: When a fold does not finish

ops.kind: failing to close the ventral wall gives

views.narration: Three lesions, one per fold. Cranial wall fails and the heart is outside the chest — ectopia cordis, and in full form the pentalogy of Cantrell. The diaphragm fails to close behind the septum transversum and bowel enters the chest — a Bochdalek hernia, where the killer is the hypoplastic lung, not the hole. And deficient mesoderm at the tail end gives caudal regression, from sacral agenesis to sirenomelia, classically with poorly controlled maternal diabetes. Learn the fold and the lesion comes free.

claims.claim: the heart lies clear OUTSIDE the body wall
the herniated bowel reaches cranial of the septum transversum, into the chest
and caudal regression has removed a fifth of the embryo's length

views.title: The two cranial lesions, close up
views.narration: Both of the cranial failures happen in the same small region, so look at it on its own. The heart sits outside a ventral wall that never closed; behind and below it, bowel has climbed through a gap left in the back corner of the septum transversum. One is a hole in the wall in front of the heart and the other is a hole in the floor beneath it, and a picture of the whole embryo is too small to tell them apart.
views.new_narration: Added by the 2026-09-30 re-author, and not for teaching reasons but for measured ones: on the whole-embryo clinical beat the scene-visibility walk put ectopia cordis at 0.222% of the frame and the septum transversum at 0.205%, both under the 0.3% a structure a beat POINTS AT must reach. The lesions are small and the truncated body of caudal regression is large, so one camera cannot serve all three. RENDER-STANDARD: where two claims want incompatible cameras, that is two beats. Beat 9 keeps its narration word for word and waives those two structures TO THIS BEAT.

claims.claim: the heart lies clear outside the body wall
and the bowel has reached cranial of the septum transversum

The mismatch is therefore RECORDED, not open: deferred_modes carries [sequence, diagram], which is the same field and the same convention nine other scenes in this corpus state verbatim — 'stays first in preferred_modes and is recorded in deferred_modes ... with no curriculum edit' (brachial-artery, axillary-artery, axillary-vein, axillary-lymph-nodes, brachial-plexus, breast-mammary-gland, peritoneum-mesentery, pleura-pleural-cavity, median-ulnar-radial-nerves; checked in this run — each of those defers 3d_anatomy and builds a listed mode, so this scene uses the field in the mirror direction). CURRICULUM.json is deliberately NOT edited, by that same convention. Both views the curriculum does require, mechanism and cross_section, are present. REWORDED 2026-10-01 taking review round 1 finding 2: the previous text called the resolution 'a decision for a human, not for this run', which told every future reviewer this item was blocked when it was not — which is how an item goes quiet while looking healthy.

THE AXIS CONVENTION IS NOT PROVED BY THIS MODEL. It is a median-plane subject, so every structure it draws is mirror-symmetric in x apart from the Bochdalek defect, and the acceptance row that asserts that defect lies on the embryo's LEFT is the same statement as the declaration rather than a check on it — RENDER-STANDARD's 'a declared axis is not a proved one, and a symmetric model cannot prove its own'. The convention is carried by that rule's route (b), viz-training/tools/prove-corpus-axes.mjs, against BodyParts3D right/left pairs. A student IS marked wrong for the side of a Bochdalek hernia, so this is recorded rather than assumed.

UNITS. The model is in its own units, not anatomical millimetres, so this scene must not mix the procedural provider with bodyparts3d until something reconciles scale (engine__unit-reconciliation). No structure here carries a bodyparts3d ref.

WHAT IS SOLVED AND WHAT IS PRESCRIBED. Solved, by bisection against three statements this scene's own narration makes: where the head fold's curvature is centred and how strong it is (so that the oropharyngeal membrane becomes the most cranial point AND the cranial strip turns through half a turn), and the tail fold's amplitude (so that the cloacal membrane comes to face ventrally). Prescribed, and therefore chosen rather than derived: that the growth differential is two gaussians and how WIDE they are — so how tight the folds look is a modelling choice, though how far they turn is not; how much the midline lengthens; the schedule by which the gut's communication with the yolk sac closes; the amnion's whole aperture schedule; and the size schedule of the brain vesicles.

THE BRAIN DOES NOT CAUSALLY DRIVE THE FOLD IN THIS MODEL, and beat 1's narration says it drives it. That is the largest thing here asserted in words and not in geometry. What IS geometry is the LINK: the vesicles are placed relative to the SOLVED centre of the head fold's curvature, so the neural tube's widest station and the fold's tightest station are the same station and move together — acceptance row P1. Growing the vesicles does not bend the sheet.

THE PERICARDIAL CAVITY IS DRAWN AS AN OPENED SAC. A closed one would hide the heart it contains, and a sleeve left open at its ends would be the lit annulus RENDER-STANDARD forbids, so it carries a permanent window on the embryo's left. The coelom and its partitioning belong to 'Body cavity (coelom)' and are not claimed here.

THREE STRUCTURES SHARE GEOMETRY WITH ANOTHER AT A DIFFERENT STAGE OR VARIANT, DELIBERATELY. flat_disc is the trunk body wall pinned at t = 0 and result_shape is the same part following the view; sagittal_frame is that same part with the hemisection variant, which IS what 'cut it in the median plane' means; head_order_before and head_order_after are the cranial strip pinned at t = 0 and t = 1, which is the before/after pair the original gaps[] asked an artist for. None of them is a second copy of a bone: they are one part at two instants, which is what a procedural model is for.

THE CRANIAL STRIP IS A TEACHING DEVICE, NOT AN ANATOMICAL STRUCTURE. head_order_before and head_order_after resolve to a slender rod running along the midline from the oropharyngeal membrane to the cranial edge. It is the strip the narration tells a student to rotate; the four things ON it — septum transversum, pericardial cavity, heart, membrane — are separate structures and are what actually reverse. Declared so nobody reads the rod as a named embryonic part.

CAUDAL REGRESSION IS AN ABSENCE AND IS DRAWN AS ONE. Its ref is the TRUNK body wall built with the +regression variant — the same wall, truncated — because a lesion of deficiency has no geometry of its own to point at. In that variant the tail-fold segment, hindgut, cloaca, cloacal membrane, allantois and connecting stalk resolve to no geometry at all, which is the lesion. The first version of this scene pointed the structure at the tail-fold segment and would have shown a student 'there is no model of this structure'.

AT t = 0 THE VITELLINE DUCT IS NOT A DUCT. The whole endodermal trough is open to the yolk sac, so the part is drawn at the trough's own width, capped at the yolk sac's own radius so it does not swallow the sac it opens into. The NARROWING that beat 7 claims is measured from the communication window's own built station span, never from that capped radius.

THE VENTRAL WINDOWS ARE AIMED AT A WORLD DIRECTION, NOT AT THE LOCAL ONE. render-kit resolves a cutaway's angle per row from a world direction; the body's own ventral direction rotates along the fold. Each window is given the ventral normal at the middle of its own span, and every window in this scene is short enough in s that the error at its edges is a few degrees. The hemisection is exempt: its direction is +x, which is this model's binormal at every station and at every t, because the midline is planar by construction.

BEAT 1 STANDS AT t = 0, THE BOUNDARY. check-beat-claims displaces each beat by +/- 0.05 and +/- 0.15 and requires a claim to break at each; for this beat only the positive displacements exist. Two of its three claims break at +0.05. Beat 9's regression claim is t-INDEPENDENT by construction — the lesion is a fixed material truncation — and pins nothing; the other two claims on that beat do the pinning.

THE THREE LESIONS ARE SITED CORRECTLY AND ARE NOT FULL ANATOMICAL ACCOUNTS. Ectopia cordis is drawn as the heart outside a cranial ventral wall defect; the other four components of the pentalogy of Cantrell are named in the narration and not modelled. The Bochdalek defect is a posterolateral gap in the septum transversum with a bowel loop through it; the pleuroperitoneal membranes, the body wall contribution and the hypoplastic lung are not built, and the lung is what actually kills the baby. Caudal regression is a truncation; sirenomelia is named in the narration and not modelled.

NOT CLAIMED, unchanged from the sequence version: 'Primitive gut tube', 'Body cavity (coelom)' and 'Lateral folding' are each their own curriculum entry. The foregut, midgut and hindgut are named here because the folds are what create them; the regional derivatives, the arterial supply by gut division and the vitelline duct anomalies belong to the gut-tube entry. Diaphragm development is carried only as far as the septum transversum's journey and the C3-C4-C5 innervation.

Day numbers are the standard teaching approximations — folding through week 4, essentially complete by about day 28 — and the narration gives them as approximations, because no exam turns on the exact day of folding.

BEATS 3 AND 4 PIN ONE STRUCTURE AT ANOTHER STAGE ON PURPOSE. head_order_before is the cranial strip at t = 0 and head_order_after the same part at t = 1, drawn side by side on beat 3 and walked through on beat 4, because that is what 'draw both panels side by side and the reversal teaches itself' means and it cannot be done with one stage. It is declared in each view's pinned_ok with its reason, so check-beat-claims reports it rather than counting it as a defect — a waiver is an argument someone wrote down. Both beats' claims are evaluated at t = 1.

THE DISC IN BEAT 1 IS DRAWN OPENED IN THE MEDIAN PLANE, like the rest of this scene. flat_disc was first the closed body wall at t = 0, and the scene-visibility walk then reported driver_growth — the brain vesicles, which beat 1 HIGHLIGHTS as the entire mechanism of folding — at 0% of the frame on both measures: the part the beat is about was inside an opaque disc. It is now the same geometry with the hemisection variant, so the neural tube and its vesicles are directly visible. The label, the terms and the narration are unchanged.

BEAT 1 IS THE ONE BEAT THAT IS NOT A MEDIAN-PLANE VIEW, and it is deliberate. It looks at the flat disc face on from the ventral side, which is how every textbook draws a trilaminar disc and is what lets a student see the neural plate running down the midline with its broad cranial end. Measured rather than chosen: from `lateral` the brain vesicles that this beat HIGHLIGHTS as the entire mechanism of folding were 0.204% of the frame against the 0.3% a pointed-at structure must reach, because a lateral camera sees a flat disc edge on. From `anterior` they are 0.333% and the disc itself goes from 2.7% to 7.7%. Every other beat is `lateral`, as the scene's camera.framing says, and the narration's 'this scene follows the median plane' is about the two folds, which begin at beat 2.

BEAT 3 IS THE ONE BEAT WHOSE COMPOSITION WAS CHANGED AFTER LOOKING AT IT RATHER THAN MEASURING IT. The scene-visibility walk passed it, and the picture was still poor: COMPARE_STRUCTURES' 'side-by-side' layout is NOT implemented as a translation in viz3d.js (~1913) — it ghosts the rest and moves nothing — so the before-strip was drawn at its own t = 0 position, a bare rod alone at one edge of the frame with a void between it and the folded embryo. The flat disc at t = 0 is now drawn with it, so the before-panel is a panel. The two panels are still not laid out side by side by the player; they are the two things in their own places, which for this subject is honest — the strip really does end up where it ends up — but an author expecting a two-panel plate should know that is not what the op gives them. ROUND 3, 2026-10-01: it was changed again, and this time ON a measurement. Round 2 found that the beat drew the four NAMED things — septum transversum, pericardial cavity, cardiogenic area, oropharyngeal membrane — in their AFTER positions only, ghosted at 0.10, while the narration's first sentence recited their BEFORE order; the model was right and the picture carried one order. Four structures pinned @0 were added (before_septum, before_pericardium, before_heart, before_oropharyngeal) and the four at t = 1 were brought into COMPARE_STRUCTURES so both panels are lit, each declared in pinned_ok. MEASURED ON THE DRAWN PIXELS in the real player by viz-training/tools/probe-beat3-order-on-screen.mjs: before panel top-down septum y 94.9, heart 179.1, membrane 276.8; after panel membrane 204.5, heart 248.7, septum 346.5; panels 166 px apart with no overlap. The same probe run against the pre-fix scene fails on exactly the rows the finding named, so it is a measure of the picture and not of the model.

THE TRACED BEATS GET NO PER-VIEW CAMERA FIT, AND THAT IS AN ENGINE ITEM, NOT A SCENE ONE. applyView() in viz3d.js computes `var traced = ops.some(TRACE_STRUCTURE)` and calls frameView(700) only `if (!traced)`, so every beat carrying a trace is framed by whatever the trace's own flyTo last did. Review round 1 reported this as beat 3 being 'the only beat in the scene that never gets a per-view camera fit'; MEASURED IN THIS RUN with the repo's own gate, that is not so — beats 5 and 6 of the nine-beat version traced too, and measure-view-framing.mjs FAILED beat 6 outright with 'clipped at rest' (edgeTouch true), a failing view the review did not report, while beat 5 came second-worst at fillW 9.9 / fillH 18.7. What this run changed at the scene level is op ORDER: on every traced beat ROTATE_TO_VIEW now runs BEFORE TRACE_STRUCTURE, so the trace's own flyTo holds the newest camera ticket instead of having it taken back by a rotation standing after it. That is a scene edit and it is all a scene can do here. The merge-instead-of-replace fix to trace()'s `state.hi = {}` / `state.only = [waypoint]`, and a framing pass for traced views, are engine items: viz3d.js is under every model in the corpus and a build session has been live in this repo during each of the last two runs. Logged in REPAIR-BACKLOG.md.

THE FOUR THINGS THE NARRATION NAMES ARE THREE LEVELS ON SCREEN, AND THAT IS ANATOMY. The first sentence lists septum transversum, pericardial cavity, cardiogenic area, oropharyngeal membrane — but the pericardial cavity IS the space the cardiogenic area lies in, so the two share a station on the strip at every t (model centroids at t = 0: heart y 1.2660, pericardium 1.2640; at t = 1: 1.0892 and 1.1092). The before/after ordering on beat 3 is therefore asserted over three levels, and the cavity is asserted the other way round — CO-LOCATED with the heart, within a tolerance of the panel's own drawn height (measured 3.7 px of a 43.9 px tolerance on the before panel, 5.6 of 41.4 on the after one). That is a statement that can fail; leaving the cavity out of the ordering silently would not be.

BEAT 3'S COMPARISON STRIPS ARE NOW BEHIND THE STRUCTURES THEY CARRY, AND THAT IS THE PRICE OF THE ROUND-3 FIX, PINNED AT ITS MEASURED SIZE. With the eight structures lit, head_order_after falls to 0.006% of the frame on measure-scene-visibility's id-pick — it is behind the opaque heart — and clears on the alpha-aware with/without measure at 0.436%, peak 241 of 255, over the 0.3% floor; head_order_before is 0.328% on the id-pick. Both are still subject and still framed. The strips are a teaching marker (gaps[7]) and BEAT 4 is the beat that walks one through the fold, with the strip as its only subject. If a later round wants the strips to read as strongly as the structures on beat 3, that is a third split, not a brighter rod.

COLOUR SEPARATION IS NOT IN ANY STANDARD AND THIS SCENE HAD THE CORPUS'S ONLY REAL COLLISION. Review round 3 compared, in CIE Lab dE76, every pair of structures DRAWN IN THE SAME BEAT across all 146 scenes: 4522 pairs. 65 pairs share a colour to dE < 0.5, and 64 of them are deliberate — left/right pairs (l_pa/r_pa, phrenic_l/phrenic_r, vis_l/vis_r), the D-loop/L-loop comparison pairs in cardiac-looping, and continuous segments of one vessel in fetal-circulation. The 65th was this scene: cloaca and stalk_ventral were BOTH #2e86c1, dE 0.0, drawn together on beat 6, whose narration names them as two of its three separate exam answers — the terminal hindgut becoming the cloaca, and the connecting stalk swinging onto the belly. They are endodermal gut and extraembryonic mesoderm, they touch (the allantois runs from the one into the other), and viz3d.js paint() writes s.color over the material AND onto the chip dot (lines 2427, 2436), so the two were one colour in the picture and one colour in the list. CORRECTED by review round 3 to the model's OWN declared colour for that part, LAYERS.stalk = 0xc8a08a, which the scene had been overriding; minimum same-beat separation goes 0.0 -> 42.0 on beat 6 and 7.9 -> 26.0 on beats 2 and 7. NOT CORRECTED, because choosing new colours is a palette decision and not a forced repair: beat 6 still draws tail_fold, hindgut, cloaca and the cloacal membrane as four blues separated by only dE 7.9-11.6, and beats 9 and 10 draw ectopia_cordis against cdh at dE 9.8 and, on beat 10, heart against ectopia_cordis at dE 3.7 — on the one beat that exists to tell the two cranial lesions apart. PROPOSED RULE for RENDER-STANDARD, since no standard would have caught this: structures drawn in the same beat must differ by at least dE 15 unless they are the same structure on two sides, one structure at two stages, or two segments of one continuous thing — and a visibility floor expressed as AREA does not catch it, because two structures can each fill the frame and still be one shape to a student.

THE FOUR 'BEFORE' LABELS ASSERTED A RANK THE MODEL DOES NOT DRAW, AND THIS SCENE'S OWN gaps ENTRY SAID SO. The round-2 rework added before_septum/before_pericardium/before_heart/before_oropharyngeal and labelled the middle two 'second from the cranial edge' and 'third from the cranial edge' — while the entry above them states that the pericardial cavity IS the space the cardiogenic area lies in and is asserted CO-LOCATED with it, not ordered above it. Review round 3 re-measured it off actual mesh vertices in a fresh vm rather than taking either account: at t = 0 the vertex-box centres are septum y 1.4550, heart 1.2660, pericardium 1.2633, oropharyngeal 1.0350 — the pericardium is 0.0027 CAUDAL to the heart, under 1% of the heart's own 0.3176 y-extent, so the two labels ranked them in the order opposite to the one drawn. CORRECTED: both labels now name the structure and its relation without claiming an ordinal position. The narration, which recites four names, is original-author text and is untouched; the four-names-three-levels compression is the entry above.
